name: Mountain Athlete Strength
subtitle: 12 weeks of full-body strength, power and trail running

zones.name: Threshold-oriented
zones.cue: Hard and controlled, a few words

items.cue: Remaining time: equipment setup.

items.text: Set the rack safeties with the unloaded bar first, and unrack yourself only with a load you can control.
No suitable rack or safeties: use an appropriate DB or machine variation (goblet or belt squat, leg press, DB or machine press), keep the pattern, and set a fresh load.
Use a fixed bar, a stable step to enter and exit, and assistance you can set up alone.
Otherwise use an assisted pull-up machine or a pulldown, and log it separately.

Keep the 2–5 clean-rep target until all four sets are clean and within effort, then add one total rep across the four sets at the next exposure. At four clean sets of five, add a small load or reduce assistance and return to a lower target. Stop before kipping or technical failure.
Single-leg strength
Needs stable rear-foot support and a wall, with DBs you can manage alone — the wall is support, not a helper. Rest includes setting up the next round safely.
Complementary strength

items.cue: About 2 min of specific light preparation, then work sets starting every 3 min. A moderate secondary exposure after single-leg work — not another max test.

items.text: If 2 min isn't enough specific preparation, extend it and drop the second set rather than rush.
Calf + trunk
Ab wheel and hanging raises need independent entry and controlled execution. Otherwise use a suitable floor trunk variation or a DB calf raise.

set.name: Uphill repeats
set.text: {reps} × (1 min uphill at controlled Z4 effort + 90 s easy recovery)

flags.text: Use repeatable effort rather than chasing heart rate on short intervals. These are controlled repetitions, not all-out sprints — pick a runnable gradient with repeatable mechanics.

If the return to the start of the hill takes longer, extend the recovery and take equal time out of the easy running, or drop whole repetitions. Never rush a descent to meet the clock. If quality work is unsuitable today, run easy — no make-up intervals.

items.cue: Remaining time: station preparation.

items.text: Power

items.cue: Drop, retrieve and reset each rep.
Fast press-up, no hand release.

items.text: Needs a gym-approved wall and a wall-throw-rated ball with a clear rebound and retrieval area. Throw from chest height, let the ball drop, retrieve it yourself and fully reset every rep — no partner or catch is needed. Retrieval counts toward the time. If neither is suitable for you, omit this slot.

Single-leg strength
Slightly lower effort than Monday to fit the full session. If it runs long, extend it and shorten the WOD first.

items.rx: Even minutes · 6 controlled · finish in 25–40 s

items.text: If recovery time disappears, reduce reps, load or distance.
